title: Subsets II
statement: The list may contain duplicates. Return all UNIQUE subsets (no two with the same multiset of values), in any order.

hints.1_question: Equal values create identical subsets if you choose them in different 'positions'. How can you force a fixed way of choosing among equals?
hints.2_nudge: Sort the array. At one level of recursion, don't start a branch with a value equal to the previous sibling.
hints.3_big_hint: Sort. In the loop over i from start: if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue.

known_bugs.name: no duplicate handling
known_bugs.code:
def subsetsWithDup(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    res, cur = [], []
    def bt(start):
        res.append(cur[:])
        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            cur.append(nums[i])
            bt(i + 1)
            cur.pop()
    bt(0)
    return res
known_bugs.followup: For [1, 2, 2], how many times does the subset [1, 2] appear?

known_bugs.name: skip rule without sorting
known_bugs.followup: In [2, 1, 2] the equal values are not neighbours. What do you need to do first?

known_bugs.name: skip condition i > 0 instead of i > start
known_bugs.followup: For [1, 2, 2], the subset [2, 2] needs the second 2 to be picked after the first. Does your skip rule allow that?

followups: Why is the condition i > start and not i > 0?
